body: Microsoft: Maria Angelidou-Smith will join as CEO of Mojang and Minecraft, moving over from Reddit, where she was chief product officer.

Skydance: Former Activision Blizzard CEO Bobby Kotick has been named to the board of Skydance Corp, which now controls Paramount and Warner Bros, according to Kotaku. Kotick left Activision Blizzard at the end of 2023 following its sale to Microsoft.

articles.title: Supercell completes full acquisition of Metacore
articles.summary: Supercell has completed its acquisition of Metacore, taking 100% ownership of the Merge Mansion maker. The deal has brought Metacore’s games team into the fold, having "officially started their journey as Supercellians" supported by Supercell peers.
body: Supercell and Metacore originally announced the planned acquisition this May, when Supercell’s intentions to acquire the remainder of the Finnish studio and its flagship game went public. Supercell was already Metacore’s largest shareholder.
Alongside the purchase, Metacore announced it would be cutting up to 160 roles in Finland as part of a restructuring effort.

Months later, Supercell revealed the deal had been signed and that plans for Metacore’s integration were underway. It was expected that the deal would close at the end of September, but it has ultimately taken until today, October 19th, for an official announcement.

"We can finally share that the Supercell acquisition of Metacore and Merge Mansion has been closed. Merge Mansion will transition to be part of Supercell’s game portfolio, and Metacore is now 100% owned by Supercell," Metacore posted on LinkedIn.

articles.title: Supercell brings Clash Royale to tabletop with new Kickstarter board game
articles.summary: Supercell is bringing Clash Royale to the tabletop with Clash Royale: The Grand Arena, a board game developed with Maestro Media, set to launch on Kickstarter on October 20, 2026.
body: Designed by David Gordon, Ryan Rodriguez, and TAM, the game supports two to four players who can deploy cards, attack opponents and send their towers across two lanes.
Players will compete to destroy towers and collect crowns, the player holding the most crowns in the end wins.

The tabletop adaptation aims to retain several mechanics from the mobile game, including card-based strategy. Players build eight-card decks around a chosen champion, whose evolution card remains with them throughout the game. Players can upgrade or add characters to their decks between battles.

“Clash Royale has earned its place as a leading mobile strategy game by challenging players to think tactically, adapt, and outsmart their opponents,” said Andrea Fasulo, head of licensing at Supercell. “With The Grand Arena, our ambition is to honour that competitive spirit and strategic depth, giving fans a fresh challenge worthy of the game they love.”

articles.title: Supercell confirms Squad Busters will shut down on December 14
articles.summary: Supercell has confirmed Squad Busters will be removed from the App Store and Google Play on December 1 and stop being playable on December 14. The developer said players who already have the game installed can keep playing until December 14, with all events and timers ending on that date.
body: Supercell announced the end of Squad Busters development last October, stating that it expected to close the game at some point in 2026. In-app purchases have been switched off since then, and the window to transfer purchase value to other Supercell games closed at the end of 2025.
The developer said it could not see “a clear path forward” for the game after several reworks, including its Heroes update. It said further changes would have made it almost a completely new game.

Squad Busters launched worldwide in May 2024. AppMagic estimates put its lifetime revenue at about $67.9m from 58.6m downloads, with the US accounting for 30% of spending. That works out at an estimated $1.16 in revenue per download globally.
The company has also ruled out offline play, private servers and releasing the code, saying the game contains content and characters from across its other titles.
points: Supercell has confirmed Squad Busters will be removed from the App Store and Google Play on December 1 and stop being playable on December 14.
The developer said players who already have the game installed can keep playing until December 14, with all events and timers ending on that date.
Supercell announced the end of Squad Busters development last October, stating that it expected to close the game at some point in 2026.
In-app purchases have been switched off since then, and the window to transfer purchase value to other Supercell games closed at the end of 2025.
